alias_note
Z.ai serves GLM models through the Claude Code executable pointed at Z.ai's Anthropic-compatible endpoint. The executable never makes the output Claude's: the lane, the contact family (Z.ai), and the result provider stay zai. The production native CLI and the earlier Lite trial contact are two contacts of one lane; the trial contact never creates production credit or a second quota.

summary
Assignment-scoped implementation, tests, research, and tool use, and independent review of other providers' work when Z.ai did not materially author the candidate; never self-review. GLM output served through the Claude Code executable is attributed to Z.ai and is never relabelled Claude. The lane holds a Director-invited committee seat with the owner-approved advisory weight 1.5 (total 10.0 for new debates), and a nonzero allocation target is not evidence that it is operational: it stays closed until every production readiness check passes.

Capabilities

summary
Tool-enabled GLM agent work through the Claude Code executable on Z.ai's Coding Plan endpoint, limited to the packet's grants and to client-side coding tools: repository reading, fixed test runners (also in review assignments), and isolated-branch edits confined to owned paths only when ZAI_ALLOW_REPOSITORY_WRITE is true. The tool limits are Claude Code permission rules, not an operating-system sandbox. Web search is not advertised: a generic Claude tool name is not evidence that Z.ai supports it. Eligible independent reviewer of candidates it did not author. It performs no external effect, and media capabilities of individual GLM models are not wired or advertised.
strengths
  • text coding and tool-enabled agent work within granted tools
  • test execution through fixed test runners, including for independent review
  • repository research within granted read tools
  • independent review of candidates it did not author

not_modeled_note
The route is the GLM Coding Plan subscription through native Claude Code: $0 additional API cash is allocated to it, and the owner's $5 total ceiling and historical holds are unchanged. Three quantities stay distinct and none is invented: incremental cash expense (usage.cost_usd, null because a call measures no charge; confirm against the account), Coding Plan credits (not reported by the CLI; read from the account), and the CLI's model-equivalent dollar telemetry at Anthropic tariffs (reported as a risk line, not a charge). The packet's per-attempt budget and token limits, the shared absolute cutoff, and the turn cap bound each attempt.

Credential environment

primary_lane_allowlist

host_bridge_allowlist

settings_credential_fields
  • zai_api_key
values_policy
names_and_booleans_only_never_values
child_environment_rule
Nothing is inherited by name. The child starts from the lane-minimal base environment with every ANTHROPIC_* and CLAUDE_* variable removed; the transport then injects the Z.ai key explicitly as the child's ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, pins the base URL and every model slot, and points home and config at a throwaway per-attempt directory. On the host bridge only the bridge process reads ZAI_API_KEY (forwarded from its profile), refuses a key whose key-ID SHA-256 differs from the command map's, and never passes that name to a child. No other lane's credential reaches a Z.ai process.

Platform limitations

  • limitation
    The Docker Director reaches the Windows Claude Code CLI only through the authenticated host bridge, whose zai entry runs the same GLM-verifying native transport in the bridge process; the container holds neither the key nor the CLI.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/host_provider_bridge.py:WindowsHostProviderExecutor
  • limitation
    Excluded from the legacy engine, which remains a supported rollback path: its worker contract is assignment text to ProviderRun with no v1 packet, and the only route to the Windows CLI is the host bridge, which verifies the primary Postgres writer fence before launch while rollback disables that writer. A legacy Z.ai worker would need the CLI inside the container or a weakened fence. Firecrawl, GitHub Copilot and OpenAI production likewise have no legacy worker.
    source
    docs/langgraph-primary-operations.html, Rollback; src/director_orchestrator/providers.py:provider_registry
  • limitation
    A Z.ai debate turn runs only in the primary runtime, when the owner's explicit DIRECTOR debate command invites it through the Slack gateway, which signs the parsed invitation for /v1/intake to verify. The Director is always seated beside it for its own position and 2.5 vote; each seat is one POSITION assignment dispatched like any other, and the live evidence phase tallies the validated contributions over the fixed 10.0 total (Director and Z.ai alike: 4.0), listing uninvited members as not seated and failing closed without the Director's contribution. Primary tasks hold no rebuttal round, and legacy intake refuses an invitation (409) rather than drop the Z.ai seat.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/primary_committee.py; src/director_orchestrator/slack_bot.py:_forward; src/director_orchestrator/primary_default.py:build_primary_committee_resolver
  • limitation
    No protected signing: Z.ai is not a native acceptance issuer, a v2 issuer family, or a qualified v3 review product. It is recognized as a material-author family, so its candidates bind reviewer independence; ordinary non-author review eligibility is unaffected.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/native_acceptance_issuer.py:ROLE_PROVIDERS
  • limitation
    Tool limits are Claude Code permission rules on an ordinary host process, not an operating-system sandbox. Web search is not advertised on this route, and no MCP server is installed.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/zai_native.py:tool_arguments
  • limitation
    Only a Director refusal before signing, or the bridge's signed refusal (first answer or replay of the recorded reason), is a proven no-run settled as refused before I/O; any unsigned or unreadable bridge error stays ambiguous and is never replayed.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/host_provider_bridge.py:BridgeClaimStore; src/director_orchestrator/primary_default.py:bridge_refusal_no_run_hold
  • limitation
    Qualification is pending and belongs to the integration owner: historical failed or ambiguous attempts stay held and are never replayed; the subscription-only canary runs once after independent review and admission.
    source
    docs/provider-setup.html, Z.ai production lane
  • limitation
    Completion of the enrollment needs a real authorized Slack thread response and receipt through the existing Director relay; installing configuration is not completion.
    source
    docs/provider-setup.html, Z.ai production lane
  • limitation
    usage.cost_usd is null for every attempt: a call measures no cash charge, plan credits are not reported by the CLI, and the CLI's dollar figure is model-equivalent telemetry at Anthropic tariffs, not a charge.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/zai_native.py:accounting_notes
  • limitation
    The lane exists only from explicit configuration and readiness; it is never discovered on PATH, where the same executable is the Claude lane.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/primary_transports.py:discover_local_primary_command_transports
  • limitation
    Media capabilities of individual GLM models are not wired or advertised; the lane is text coding and tool-enabled agent work only.
    source
    docs/provider-setup.html, Z.ai production lane
  • limitation
    The Lite trial contact is trial-only: a separate append-only trial ledger, no production credit, no counted review verdict, and no dispatch at or after the trial end or in production mode.
    source
    src/director_orchestrator/zai_lane.py; src/director_orchestrator/config.py:validate_zai_trial_configuration

    authority_note
    The only transport that may serve the zai lane, run in-process by a host deployment (ZAI_TRANSPORT=native) or by the Windows host bridge for the Docker Director. It runs one validated packet per attempt with packet-scoped tool grants, refuses every external effect before launch, and accepts only a complete successful envelope served by the configured GLM model; configuration alone never makes the lane callable.
    current_transport_constraints
    • composed locally only with ZAI_TRANSPORT=native and every zai_production readiness boolean
    • tool grants limited to READ_REPOSITORY, RUN_TESTS, and WRITE_ISOLATED_BRANCH; any other grant, including PUBLIC_WEB_SEARCH, is refused before launch
    • RUN_TESTS or writes run in default permission mode with only the listed rules; pure reads run in plan mode; never a bypass mode; print mode cannot wait on a permission prompt
    • WRITE_ISOLATED_BRANCH needs ZAI_ALLOW_REPOSITORY_WRITE and owned paths; .env files, .git, and prohibited paths are always denied
    • turns capped by ZAI_MAX_TURNS; the shared absolute cutoff and contained process tree apply, and a nonzero exit stays ambiguous
    • missing token counts mean the result is never SUCCEEDED; cash cost is recorded as null, never zero

Communication

relay_rule
provider_messages_relay_through_director
direct_provider_to_provider_channels_exist
false
notes
  • Z.ai reaches every other lane only through Director-authored packets, declared dependency outcomes, review handoffs, and Director-invited advisory debate turns dispatched as primary work packets and tallied at weight 1.5.
  • Z.ai never posts to Slack; the Director relays a concise assignment-correlated summary through the existing Slack thread relay, preserving thread_ts.
  • Trial-lane results never reach another provider as production evidence.
